message:
Both drafts are feasible: each has 13 credits (within your 12–16 limit), includes required CAP4000 and lab 90010, retains protected sections 90001/90002, and has no class or work conflicts. Your CS3000 grade of B satisfies CAP4000’s prerequisite alternative; CS3500 is not also required.

Plan A: CAP4000 meets Mon/Wed 8:00–9:15 a.m. Classes span three days: Mon, Wed, Thu. This keeps classes off Tuesday but requires early starts.

Plan B: CAP4000 meets Tue/Thu 10:00–11:40 a.m., leaving 20 minutes before your noon–5:00 p.m. work shifts. Classes span four days, but mornings start later.

Both include Thursday lab 5:30–6:20 p.m., 30 minutes after work. Neither fully matches your afternoon-class preference, which is a preference rather than a hard constraint. Both studio sections and the lab currently have available seats; drafting does not reserve them.

A and B are drafted only. Nothing has been saved or registered; your enrollment is unchanged.
